fair_value.method: Blend of 40x forward 2028E EPS of $6.50 (my extrapolation; no FY28 consensus exists) = $260 (50%), 8x 2028E EV/sales on ~$9.0B plus ~$2.45B equity-adjusted net cash = $230 (25%), and a 10-year DCF (WACC 10.5%, 19% mature FCF margin, 3.5% terminal) plus the same net cash = $157 (25%), all as of Sep 2027 on ~324M diluted shares (in-the-money 0% 2030 converts treated as equity); blended ~$227 vs $288.7 last close.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028E non-GAAP EPS $6.50, my own extrapolation (+32% on FY27 consensus $4.93 on $6.79B revenue, 28 analysts, range $2.95-$7.01; FY26 guide $2.55-2.85) x 40x forward P/E (PEG ~1.1-1.3 for 30-40% EPS growth; premium to power/industrial peers at 25-35x). EPS already on a diluted basis that includes convert shares, so no balance-sheet adjustment.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: 2028E revenue ~$9.0B (FY26 ~$4.05-4.1B, +55-65% 2027 to ~$6.3-6.8B, +35-40% 2028) x 8x EV/sales = ~$72B EV; + ~$2.45B equity-adjusted net cash ($2.67B cash at 6/30/26 less ~$0.2B financing obligations; the ~$2.475B of converts, conversion ~$194.97, treated as equity) = ~$74.5B equity; / ~324M diluted shares (Q2 diluted 323.3M includes conversion shares)

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue from ~$4.05B (2026) growing 55%/40%/30%/25%/20%/16%/12%/9%/6%/4% to ~$26.8B in 2035; FCF margin ramps 10% -> 19%; WACC 10.5%; terminal growth 3.5%; EV ~$48.5B as of Sep 2027 + ~$2.45B net cash = ~$51B; / ~324M diluted shares

bear.story: AI capex digestion or financing stress at neocloud/Oracle-linked projects; Project Jupiter slips past 2028 because the Green Chile pipeline (state trust-land right-of-way denied twice; Energy Transfer in-service target moved to ~Feb 1, 2027) or the fuel-cell air-quality permit (NMED decision reportedly due by Nov 23, 2026, hearings only just un-stayed by the NM Supreme Court) fails, and Bloom cannot redeploy the units fast enough; Feb 2027 FY27 guide lands well below ~$6.8B consensus revenue; short-report issues (scandium, degradation) gain traction; multiple compresses to ~30x on ~$4.5-5 FY27/28 EPS, cushioned slightly by ~$7.5/share of net cash.

base.story: 2026 delivered at ~$4.1B, FY27 guided ~$6.5B+ with ~34-36% gross margin and 2 GW Fremont capacity ramping; Jupiter proceeds with some slip but the ~$8B+ equipment backlog (Morgan Stanley estimate, more than half non-Oracle) and financing-partner purchase terms keep shipments flowing; EPS estimates keep rising modestly while the multiple compresses from ~59x FY27 toward ~40x FY28, leaving the stock roughly flat with large interim swings.

bull.story: Jupiter permits clear and the 2.4 GW Oracle contract ships on schedule, the rest of the 2.8 GW Oracle framework plus new hyperscaler/Brookfield/Aligned GW-scale awards land, capacity expansion beyond 2 GW is announced, FY27 revenue beats $7B and 2028 EPS heads to $9+; the market keeps paying 50x+ for scarce behind-the-meter power.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$145 (-50%, well under the ~$164 post-Q2 low of late July) BE would trade at ~29x FY27 consensus EPS of $4.93 even with ~$7.5/share of net cash, which is only consistent with a real fundamental break: Project Jupiter actually cancelled or deferred past 2028 (air permit denied or the pipeline stuck well beyond Feb 2027, without redeployment of the units to other Oracle or third-party sites), a Feb 2027 FY27 guide far below ~$6.8B revenue, gross margin back under ~30%, validation of the fuel-cell degradation or China-scandium allegations (supply disruption, warranty costs, SEC action), or a broad AI data-center capex retrenchment. With 112% realized vol, $170-230 can be ordinary noise; $145 most likely would not be.

Wide analyst dispersion: FY27 EPS range $2.95-$7.01; price targets from ~$97 to $390 (recent: Mizuho $351, Clear Street $330, Morgan Stanley $310, Jefferies $229), mean ~$280
reasoning: Round 2 revision. Bloom Energy (BE) re-rated from ~$60 to ~$289 on AI data-center behind-the-meter power: Q2'26 revenue $1.065B (+166% y/y), non-GAAP GM 34.3%, op margin 22.5%; FY26 guide $3.9-4.2B revenue, $2.55-2.85 EPS; FY27 consensus $4.93 EPS on $6.79B revenue and rising; S&P 500 member since Sep 21. The supervisor showed I double-counted the converts: the ~$2.475B of 0% 2030 notes convert at ~$194.97, are deep in the money and already in the 323.3M Q2 diluted count, so equity-adjusted net cash is ~$2.45B (~$7.5/share) on ~324M shares. That lifts my EV/sales leg from $218 to $230 and my DCF from $148 to $157; the P/E leg is unchanged at $260 (EPS is already diluted; 2028E $6.50 is my extrapolation, not consensus). Blend moves from $222 to ~$227, still below spot. On Oracle, I accept the correction: the Sep 24 force-majeure notice runs from Oracle to developer Stack (Blue Owl) as a rent-deferral right, not a dispute with Bloom, and Bloom states Oracle remains committed to the 2.4 GW Jupiter contract (my 1.2 GW figure was the initial tranche of the 2.8 GW framework). I partly disagree with the supervisor's 'timing risk only' framing: my follow-up found the pipeline's state trust-land right-of-way was denied twice, with no disclosed reroute, and the air permit hearing process only just restarted, so a slip past 2028 is plausible. But Jupiter is not in 2026 guidance, Morgan Stanley estimates $8B+ equipment backlog with more than half non-Oracle, and modular units can be redeployed, so I keep bear weight at 25% rather than raise it; the net effect with the balance-sheet correction is a small upward nudge (base $280->$285, bear $140->$150). On the right tail, the supervisor noted mine was the thinnest; I widened it modestly (P>=577 0.07->0.083, P>=722 0.025->0.035), which is what my own mixture implies once the bull component is centred at $470 with 42% dispersion, but I stay below the peer tail because $722 (~$235B market cap) would need ~80x a $9 2028 EPS. Distribution: mixture of lognormals, bear 25% (median $150, sigma 0.42), base 50% ($285, 0.35), bull 25% ($470, 0.42), giving a median ~$280 and effective vol ~75-85%, below the 112% trailing realized vol (inflated by a 5x run and short-report shocks) but far above large-cap base rates. The far-left tail is kept fatter than the mixture (P>=72 0.97, P>=115 0.92) because the stock was $61 a year ago. Research: ~14 round-1 queries plus 5 round-2 searches/fetches; no option data used.
